deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft for Riemann's 1854 Göttingen communication 'Ueber die Gesetze der Vertheilung von Spannungselectricität in ponderabeln Körpern, wenn diese nicht als vollkommene Leiter oder Nichtleiter, sondern als dem Enthalten von Spannungselectricität mit endlicher Kraft widerstrebend betrachtet werden' (Werke, Nr. XIV). The phrase 'Widerstreben des ponderabeln Körpers gegen das electrisch Werden' on the page matches that title.

(1) Definition of the potential (left column, top). Riemann sets u(x,y,z,t) equal to 1/(4π) of the potential of all acting electric masses:
  u = (1/4π) ∫ ρ'(x',y',z',t) dx'dy'dz' / sqrt((x-x')²+(y-y')²+(z-z')²),
where ρ' is the density of 'Spannungselectricität' (free charge) at (x',y',z') at time t. He then states Poisson's equation in this normalization:
  ∂²u/∂x² + ∂²u/∂y² + ∂²u/∂z² = -ρ.
This holds because Δ(1/r) = -4π δ.

(2) The electromotive force. He assumes that, besides the ordinary electrostatic force -∂u/∂x, ..., there acts everywhere an additional electromotive force with components -β² ∂ρ/∂x, -β² ∂ρ/∂y, -β² ∂ρ/∂z. The right column writes the total x-component as -∂u/∂x - β² ∂ρ/∂x. Hence the total force is -∇(u + β²ρ).

(3) Reinterpretation as scalar 'causes'. Instead of a force with components -β²∇ρ, one may assume at each point an electromotive 'Ursache' (cause) of intensity β²ρ. It tends to diminish the density of like electricity, i.e. to increase that of the opposite kind. Physically it is a resistance of the ponderable body to becoming electrified. Likewise, the force -∇u can be replaced by a cause of intensity u, which tends to diminish the density of electricity. The two scalar intensities simply add, giving u + β²ρ.

(4) Interpretive remark. With this view one need not posit two electric fluids and read ρ dx dy dz as the excess of positive over negative electricity in the element. One can essentially return to the Franklinian (one-fluid) conception without any striking extra assumption.

(5) Right column. These are reformulations of the same definition: u (the 'Spannung') at (x,y,z) at time t is 1/(4π) of the potential of the tension-electricity, with ρ'dx'dy'dz' the tension-electricity of the element at time t. A struck-out start reads 'das Gesetz für die Bewegung der Electricität in ruhenden ponderabeln Körpern scheint daran'. A closing fragment notes that u at each instant depends on all the acting masses.

Implicit consequences (mine; these appear in the published paper, not on this page):
- With Ohmic current j = -k∇(u + β²ρ) and continuity ∂ρ/∂t = -div j, one gets ∂ρ/∂t = kΔ(u + β²ρ) = k(β²Δρ - ρ).
- At equilibrium u + β²ρ = const inside the body, so β²Δρ = ρ. Charge then forms a surface layer decaying like exp(-d/β): a screening length β.
errors: No mathematical errors on the page. Poisson's equation Δu = -ρ is correct for the 1/(4π) normalization of u.

The phrase about the β²ρ cause 'vermehren' in the machine transcription conflicts with the physics. The force -β²∇ρ drives charge away from accumulations, so the cause must tend to diminish the density of like electricity (equivalently, to increase that of the opposite kind). The image supports reading the parenthesis as the 'increase the opposite' paraphrase.
Draft-level notation slips: the right column alternates between ρ and ρ' and between (x,y,z) and (x',y',z') when defining u. Riemann himself corrected these by rewriting the definition several times.

results.what: Definition u = (1/4π)∫ρ'/r dV' and Poisson's equation Δu = -ρ

Additional electromotive force -β²∇ρ, giving total force -∇(u + β²ρ). This represents a finite resistance of matter to holding free charge, leading to β²Δρ = ρ in equilibrium (charge layers of thickness β).
results.modern_name: Gradient-of-density ('diffusion-like') contribution to the electrochemical potential; screened Poisson equation and screening length, analogous to Debye-Hückel/Thomas-Fermi screening
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's 1854 paper; the modern screening theory is credited to Debye-Hückel (1923) and Thomas-Fermi (1927)

results.what: Interpretation of the forces as scalar 'causes' of intensity u and β²ρ, allowing a one-fluid (Franklinian) reading of ρ
results.modern_name: Electrochemical potential as a scalar driving quantity; one-fluid theory of electricity
results.usually_credited_to: Franklin (one-fluid theory); Riemann (this interpretive remark, 1854 context)

deep.surprise_reason: This is draft material for Riemann's published 1854 paper on the distribution of tension-electricity in bodies that resist being electrified (Werke XIV), where the β²ρ term and the resulting screening already appear. The Franklinian remark is a minor interpretive detail, and nothing goes beyond what is known as his.

Equals 0: 1/r is harmonic away from the source, consistent with Poisson's equation for u.
Equals 0: in equilibrium (u + β²ρ = const, so β²Δρ = ρ) a sphere carries a charge distribution sinh(r/β)/r concentrated near the surface on the length scale β.

transcription_corrections: 'Geradschen Potentialsumme' / 'Geradschen Potentials' is very likely a misreading. Probably 'Gauss'schen' (or possibly 'Green'schen'), referring to the potential of the acting masses.

In the sentence on the cause of intensity β²ρ, the sense (supported by the image) is: 'welche die Dichtigkeit der gleichartigen Electricität zu vermindern (d.h. die Dichtigkeit der entgegengesetzten zu vermehren) strebt'. The transcription's bare 'zu vermehren' attached to the like-kind density is likely wrong.
'einen Widerstreben ... suchen' should read roughly 'in diesen Ursachen kann man ein Widerstreben des ponderabeln Körpers gegen das electrisch Werden sehen/suchen'.
'Franklin'schen' is plausible and contextually correct (return to the one-fluid view).
In the left column, 'ohne irgend eine auffallende Annahme' is likely 'ohne irgend welche auffallende Annahme'; the meaning is unchanged.
